The ¹H NMR shows 15 total protons: a 10 H multiplet at 1.35 ppm (likely five CH₂ groups), a 1 H multiplet at 2.63 ppm (a methine coupled to the cyclohexyl protons), and an AA′BB′ aromatic pattern (4 H, 7.24 ppm and 7.41 ppm). This pattern fits a para‑disubstituted benzene where one substituent is a cyclohexyl group attached via a methine carbon (C‑H) and the opposite para position is a non‑proton‑bearing group (e.g., a carbonyl, halogen, etc.). To pinpoint the exact substituent, I’ll request the ¹³C NMR spectrum, which will reveal how many distinct carbon environments are present and whether a carbonyl or other functional group is present.</thought>
